name: Kettlebell swing
pattern: Ballistic hip hinge: the bell swings back between the legs, then a snap of the hips throws it forward to chest height.
setup: Feet a bit wider than hips, bell a foot in front of you.
Hinge, grab the handle with both hands, flat back.
Tip the bell toward you and hike it back between your thighs like a football snap.

steps.text: Bell goes high between the thighs, forearms touch the inner thighs, hips back.
Drive the hips forward hard; arms stay long and loose.
Stand tall like a plank; the bell floats to chest height.
Let the bell fall; hinge only when your arms meet your body.

cues.cue: Hinge, don't squat: hips back, shins nearly vertical.
cues.why: The hinge style gave more hamstring activity than squat-style swings.

cues.cue: At the top, glutes and abs tight, stand straight like a plank.
cues.why: The swing is fast on-off muscle pulses; a hard brace at the top protects the back.

cues.cue: Arms are ropes; the hips move the bell.
cues.why: Glute activity reaches about 80% of max with a 16 kg bell when the hips drive it.

cues.cue: Flat back at the bottom, neck long.
cues.why: Low back compression is about 3,200 N even with a 16 kg bell.

cues.cue: Go heavier as you get better, not faster and sloppier.
cues.why: Heavier bells raised hip and lumbar moments but not knee moments.

breathing: Short sharp breath out at each hip snap; breathe in as the bell drops.

mistakes.name: Squatting the swing
mistakes.looks: Knees bend deep and push forward; the bell swings low near the floor.
mistakes.fix: Push hips back, shins near vertical; bell goes between the thighs.
mistakes.why: Turns a hip drive into a squat; less hamstring work.

mistakes.name: Lifting with the arms
mistakes.looks: The shoulders shrug and the arms raise the bell like a front raise.
mistakes.fix: Relax the arms; drive with the hips.
mistakes.why: Shoulders get tired and the hips do less.

mistakes.name: Leaning back at the top
mistakes.looks: The hips push past the feet and the shoulders lean behind them.
mistakes.fix: Finish straight: squeeze glutes, ribs down.
mistakes.why: Adds spine extension at the moment of highest speed.

mistakes.name: Back rounds at the bottom
mistakes.looks: The bell pulls the shoulders and spine forward on the backswing.
mistakes.fix: Lighter bell, hike it higher between the thighs.
mistakes.why: Loads a flexed spine at speed.

safety: Clear space in front and behind; stop the set with a controlled backswing and park the bell.
Back irritation: a few people find swings aggravate the back; reduce load or switch to hip thrusts.

variants.change: One hand: the opposite upper back muscles work about 24% harder to resist twisting.
Bell goes overhead: more shoulder range and more spine extension at the top.
Hold one dumbbell by the end; same pattern.
Band from behind or under the feet: no swing of a weight, the band resists the hip snap.
Bell swings in a diagonal arc across the body: more rotation.
Combination: swing into a catch at the chest, then squat or press.
No weight: arms swing to practise the hinge timing.

subtypes.name: Full / overhead swing
subtypes.change: Bell continues overhead, arms by the ears at the top.

subtypes.name: Side swing
subtypes.change: Bell swings past the outside of one hip and up across the body.

motion.basis: Hinge-style two-hand swing. mcgill2012 and vangelder2015 recorded sagittal motion but only muscle and load values were available here; joint angles are estimates of a typical hinge swing (bell to chest height, shoulderFlex about 90). MET 9.8 is the 2024 Compendium entry 02058 kettlebell swings.
